title: I Returned the Entitled Cart to the Parent Who Left It in Traffic

parts.text: I pushed her runaway cart back into the bumper that had launched it. I am twenty-four, barista between shifts, Costco Saturday, heat coming off asphalt. A mom, visor, yelled that I should watch her kid while she loaded twelve packs. I was not hired. The cart rolled toward a moving pickup. I grabbed it. The kid was in her SUV, belted, fine. She still wanted a lecture for me. The visor said BEACH in rhinestones that were peeling. I said the cart is yours, the kid is yours, I am a stranger with iced coffee. She called me rude to a man collecting carts, Luis, who shrugged. I put the cart on her bumper, gently. I walked away. No viral fight. The iced coffee watered down, a tragedy. Luis later said thanks for not making it his job either. Entitled is often just someone assigning you a role you did not audition for. I ate a food-court hot dog standing up, mustard on my thumb, peace. Mom said, "Can you just stand here" I said, "No. Here's your cart" The pickup driver honked once, late. That was the whole orchestra. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I put the runaway cart back on her bumper and left
